title: Harvester AudioSearch integration: field journal
content:
Context: quick capture from kickoff + tech call with Harvester (small startup building audio search for podcasts and enterprise call archives). Attendees: Maya Patel (CTO), Jiro Tanaka (Eng lead), Anika Sharma (SE, Redwood), Marcus Lee (solutions eng). Goal: scope a 6-week PoC that validates latency, recall, and a private deployment option behind customer VPC.

Call summary / what they care about:
- User story: end users paste an audio clip or search via text query; system returns short timestamped snippets with confidence and source links. Tight p95 latency target: <= 350ms for query -> top-5 snippet results for 10s query over 1M indexed segments.
- Data profile: 120k transcripts (variable length, avg 45s), some recordings have PII (names, numbers). Customers want optional redaction.
- Throughput: expected steady-state 50 qps peak for search, burst to 300 qps during big events. Cost sensitivity: want to avoid heavy per-query generator use; embeddings + ANN is primary.

Technical constraints / notes:
- Wants private deployment (VPC) with Redwood Private control plane. KMS integration mandatory (AWS KMS) and audit logs required.
- Indexing pipeline: they'll ship transcripts + time offsets via S3. Need a chunking strategy that preserves snippet boundaries. Proposed: 5–10s sliding windows with 50% overlap to improve recall at boundaries — tradeoff on index size discussed.
- Embedding model options: small fast open model (e.g., text-embedding-3-small equivalent) vs higher-quality for recall. Proposal: baseline with smaller model for cost + optional rerank using larger model for top-20 candidates.
- ANN ops: recommend HNSW index sharded across 3 nodes for 1M segments; warm-up routines required. Consider Faiss/Annoy vs vector DB managed — for Private they want self-hosted vector index on dedicated GPU/CPU nodes.
- Runtime expectations: token generation only for snippet contextualization (short). Main cost is embedding lookup + rerank.

Gotchas / risks called out in call:
- Cold-start for index shards leads to p95 spikes; need pre-warmed cache or smaller hotset cache with routing to dedicated nodes.
- Variable transcript quality; embeddings sensitive to ASR errors. Plan to evaluate noise-robust embedding and simple normalization pipeline (strip filler words, punctuation heuristics).
- PII handling: must support redaction before indexing and in results. Need clear pipeline step and proof-of-process for compliance.
- Long-tail queries (very long textual queries or multi-turn refinement) could trigger fallback to generator-based summarization — define limits and quotas.
- Storage blow-up from overlapping windows; provide cost estimates per 1M segments for 5s, 10s window sizes.

PoC success criteria (agreed):
- Recall@10 >= 0.88 on curated eval set (they will provide 1k labeled queries)
- Search latency p95 <= 350ms for top-5 on infra similar to proposed PoC cluster
- Index build for 1M segments completes within 2 hours in PoC environment
- Demonstrate KMS-backed key rotation and audit log export to their SIEM

Immediate action items / owners:
- Anika: deliver PoC runbook + infra spec (machines, networking, estimated vCPU/GPU) by 2025-11-07
- Marcus: sample index size and cost model for 5s vs 10s window (estimate storage + RAM) by 2025-11-06
- Harvester (Jiro): share 10k sample transcripts + eval queries (anonymized) to s3://harvester-samples/ by 2025-11-10
- Maya: confirm compliance checklist (PII redaction policies) and legal contact for DPA by 2025-11-12
- Create JIRA-482 to track PoC; attach evaluation scripts and dataset. Marcus to own run-of-show during demo.

Open technical decisions (to resolve in design doc):
- Which embedding model for baseline (quality vs cost). Suggest: start with fast small model; if recall < threshold then enable larger rerank step.
- ANN engine selection (Faiss on self-hosted vs managed vector DB). Tradeoffs: operational burden vs control in Private.
- Chunking overlap and dedup logic for snippet reconstruction (how to present contiguous snippets without duplicating metadata).

Notes to self / rough experiment ideas:
- Precompute low-dim float16 embeddings and test HNSW ef/construction knobs to hit p95 targets with limited RAM.
- Try one-pass hybrid: smaller embeddings for recall + cheap lexical filter to remove obvious matches before rerank.
- Measure ASR-error-robustness by corrupting transcripts with common ASR mistakes and measuring embedding drift.

Meeting next steps / scheduling:
- 2025-11-11 10:00 PT: technical design review with Harvester eng team (schedule tentative)
- 2025-11-17: infra build kickoff (if PoC signed)

Quick capture of Slack links / tickets mentioned:
- slack: #se-harvester-integration thread
- jira: JIRA-482 (PoC: harvester audio search)

Quick handoff note: keep PoC narrow — baseline embedding + ANN + simple rerank. Avoid generator-heavy flows in PoC unless they ask for summary features. Focus on reliable privacy controls and latency measurements.
